papers.abstract: We study zero-error communication and exact simulation of quantum channels assisted by quantum no-signalling correlations. For a channel with Kraus operator space $K$, we introduce a semidefinite programming parameter $\Gamma(K)$ that is exactly multiplicative under tensor products and upper-bounds $\Theta_{\rm NS}(K)$, where $\log_2\Theta_{\rm NS}(K)=C_{0,\rm NS}(K)$ and $C_{0,\rm NS}(K)$ denotes the asymptotic quantum no-signalling-assisted zero-error capacity. Among known upper bounds on $\Theta_{\rm NS}$ given by semidefinite programs, $\Gamma$ is the tightest. We also prove that the previously introduced simulation lower bound $\Sigma^{-}(K)$ is exactly multiplicative and satisfies $\Theta_{\rm NS}(K)\leq\Gamma(K)\leq\Sigma^{-}(K)\leq\Gamma(K)^2$. Using this multiplicativity, we show that neither $S_{0,\rm NS}(K)=\log_2\Sigma^{-}(K)$ nor its regularized extension $S_{0,\rm NS}(K)=\lim\nolimits_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\log_2\Sigma^{-}(K^{\otimes n})$ holds in general. This answers an open question about the asymptotic simulation cost $S_{0,\rm NS}(K)$. For classical-quantum channels, we obtain sharp bounds. If $r$ is the effective output dimension, then $\Theta_{\rm NS}\leq\Gamma\leq(1+r^{1/2})\Theta_{\rm NS}/2$ and $\Gamma\leq\Sigma^{-}\leq(1+r^{1/2})\Gamma/2$. If $k$ is the minimum rank of the output support projections, then $\Sigma^{-}/\Theta_{\rm NS}\leq[(1+r^{1/2})/(1+k^{1/2})]^2$, and this bound is sharp for every $1\leq k\leq r$. Thus, we obtain the sharp bound $S_{0,\rm NS}-C_{0,\rm NS}\leq2\log_2[(1+r^{1/2})/(1+k^{1/2})]$.
authors: Xin Li, Yinan Li

papers.title: Data-Driven Optimization of Seminumerical Exchange for SIMD CPUs
papers.abstract: We present a seminumerical exchange algorithm (SNK) based on the sn-LinK method [Laqua et al., J. Chem. Theory Comput. 16, 1456 (2020)], optimized for modern multi-core central processing units with single instruction multiple data vector instructions and report its implementation into the Q-Chem quantum chemistry program. Vectorization and memory management strategies for the Boys function and 3-center-1-electron (3c1e) integral kernels are given. Several new considerations are made in the computation of the 3c1e integrals: the Head-Gordon Pople horizontal recurrence relations, same-center optimizations, and multishell optimizations, all implemented symbolically employing the SymPy symbolic algebra library and exported as optimized C++ code leveraging common-sub-expression elimination (CSE) optimization techniques. A general scheme for choosing optimal integral kernels is developed through rigorous timing benchmarks. The resulting implementation is tested against traditional 4c2e exchange for several systems and basis sets, showing 1-2 orders of magnitude speedups for systems of practically relevant sizes (100-500 atoms, 2000-10000 basis functions). For smaller molecules, comparisons are also made against the more efficient occ-RI-K method showing a break-even point around 50-100 atoms beyond which SNK dramatically outperforms due to its superior sub-quadratic (between linear and quadratic) time complexity as well as its effectively negligible memory demand.
authors: Jesse DiCenso, Henryk Laqua, Martin Head-Gordon

papers.title: Displacement-noise-free gravitational-wave detector using quantum tomography of photon orbital angular momentum states
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) induce quantum transitions between photon orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) states with amplitudes $\alpha_{\pm}$. Exploiting this effect, we present a displacement-noise-free detection framework that extracts GW information from the OAM Hilbert space. Parametrized quantum state tomography of the GW-induced OAM sidebands enables a single V-shaped detector to resolve all seven wave parameters: the frequency, propagation direction, two polarization amplitudes, and initial phase of each polarization. Direct detection of the sidebands yields a weak signal of approximately $10^{-15}\,\mathrm{W}$. We therefore introduce a stronger reference state $r |0>_{\mathrm{P}}$, with $r=0.01$, to enhance the detected signal. For an arm length of $L=4\,\mathrm{m}$, $N=160$ round trips, a paraxial parameter of $\gamma=0.1$, an incident light power of $P_{\mathrm{BS}}=10\,\mathrm{kW}$, a wavelength of $\lambda_{\mathrm{opt}}=1064\,\mathrm{nm}$, and GW amplitudes of $A=10^{-18}$, we estimate sideband transition amplitudes of $|\alpha_{\pm}|\sim10^{-10}$ and signal powers of order $1\,\mathrm{nW}$, scaling as $P_{\mathrm{BS}}\alpha_{\pm}\propto P_{\mathrm{BS}}ANL\gamma/\lambda_{\mathrm{opt}}$. The shot-noise-limited sensitivity floor is $S^{1/2}_n=1.6\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{Hz}^{-1/2}$. Because the scheme measures OAM transition amplitudes rather than differential arm lengths, it is intrinsically free from displacement noise and provides a broadband probe of GWs, specifically bridging the $0.1$--$10\,\mathrm{Hz}$ mid-frequency gap.
authors: Haorong Wu, Xilong Fan, Lixiang Chen

papers.title: Formation of Trapped Surfaces for the Einstein-Euler System
papers.abstract: We prove the formation of trapped surfaces for the Einstein--Euler system in 3+1 dimensions beyond spherical symmetry. We consider smooth characteristic initial data in a short-pulse regime with rapid fluid injection. Starting from initial data containing no trapped surfaces, we obtain two sufficient criteria for trapped surface formation, corresponding to the shear and fluid contributions, respectively. In particular, for the fluid-driven criterion, we impose no positive lower bound on the shear flux. To handle the multiple propagation speeds associated with gravitational waves, sound waves, and fluid transport, our analysis combines three ingredients: a coercive fluid energy current whose null fluxes reflect the unequal velocity components, curvature renormalizations adapted to the matter terms, and weighted geometric estimates controlling derivatives in all spacetime directions. To ensure that fluid injection alone can lead to trapped surface formation, we use particle-number conservation in a designed spacetime region to control the focusing process and obtain the desired sphere-integrated fluxes.
authors: Xinliang An, Sifan Yu

papers.title: Localized states of the non-Hermitian Schr{\"o}dinger equation with a complex $1/r^{2}$ potential: from Efimov states to bipolarons
papers.abstract: We study the non-Hermitian Schr\"odinger equation with a complex $1/r^{2}$ potential, which bridges Hermitian few-body and non-Hermitian many-body physics: a real attractive potential describes Efimov bound states, whereas a purely imaginary one describes the medium-induced interaction between two heavy polarons at large separations. We solve this equation analytically, obtaining both the localized and continuum states, and compare the solutions with numerical and WKB results. As the imaginary part of the potential is increased, the energies of the Efimov bound states acquire imaginary parts and rotate counterclockwise in the complex plane. On approaching the purely imaginary potential, the excited states disappear sequentially, while the Efimov ground state is smoothly connected to a bipolaron state localized at short distance. Such a bipolaron is localized solely by the medium-induced imaginary interaction, without any attractive real potential. Solving the equation by finite differences, we find that each bipolaron state is necessarily accompanied by another localized state that oscillates on the scale of the mesh size and hence has no counterpart in the continuum limit. Each such pair coalesces at an exceptional point as the strength of the purely imaginary potential is varied, whereas the coalescence is lifted once a finite real part is introduced. We show that this behavior originates from a symmetry of the discretized Schr\"odinger equation that holds for any purely imaginary potential.
authors: Kyoka Tsunoda, Kazuki Yamamoto, Shimpei Endo

papers.title: Free Fermion frustration-free models have zero Hall conductance
papers.abstract: We give a new proof that translation-invariant free Fermion frustration-free models have zero Hall conductance. Our proof is analytic in nature and it uses the bulk-edge correspondence. The central argument, which holds beyond the translation-invariant situation, is that in frustration-free models, edge modes cannot merge into the ground state band. We give an example of a gapped frustration-free model that is nonetheless gapless on the half-plane.
authors: Sven Bachmann, Zhiqian Du, Martin Fraas

papers.title: Poisson statistics for one-dimensional Anderson--Bernoulli Schr\"odinger operators
papers.abstract: We prove Poisson local eigenvalue statistics for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators with nondegenerate Bernoulli potentials at any fixed nonzero coupling. After unfolding by the integrated density of states (IDS), the local eigenvalue process converges to a Poisson point process of unit intensity at every energy in the interior of the almost-sure spectrum. The theorem also holds for bounded nonconstant iid potentials, provided the IDS is continuous and strictly increasing near the reference energy. If the IDS also has a finite positive derivative at that energy, the usual linear normalization gives the same limit. The proof uses a phase coordinate with exact IDS drift to obtain a uniform exponential crossing law and joint Poisson counts in disjoint energy windows.
authors: Yi Han

papers.title: Regret Lower Bound for Online Learning of Quantum States with Logarithmic Loss, with Applications to Quantum State Tomography and Confidence Sequences for Matrix Means
papers.abstract: We study the problem of online learning of quantum states with logarithmic loss, which is a quantum generalization of online portfolio selection and has applications to quantum state tomography, the task of estimating an unknown quantum state from measurement outcomes. We first establish a regret lower bound, showing that the regret rates of Exponential Weights and the algorithm of Tseng et al. (2025) have optimal polynomial dependence on the dimension. Our analysis leads to two further results. First, our lower-bound proof leads to a quantum state tomography algorithm that is sample optimal up to polylogarithmic factors in the sample size. Second, we develop an algorithm for constructing confidence sequences for the mean of a matrix-valued random variable. A numerical experiment shows that the latter algorithm is competitive with existing methods.
authors: Yen-Huan Li, Wei-Fu Tseng

papers.title: Dynamical phase transition for a logarithm observable in chaotic systems
papers.abstract: We consider the full distribution $P_N(A)$ of the dynamical observable $A = - \sum_{i=1}^N \ln x_i$ where $x_1, \dots, x_N$ is a sequence generated by a chaotic map $f(x)$ via $x_{n+1} = f(x_n)$. We study the particular cases where $f(x)$ is the doubling, tent or logistic map, and focus on the limit $N \gg 1$. Typical fluctuations of $A$ are Gaussian with mean $\left\langle A\right\rangle$ and variance which are both of order $\sim N$. We find that the left tail of the distribution ($A < \left\langle A\right\rangle$) scales as $P_{N}(A) \sim e^{-NI(A/N)}$, and calculate the rate function $I(a)$ which depends on the map $f(x)$. Interestingly, we find that the right tail of the distribution ($A > \left\langle A\right\rangle$) follows an anomalous scaling: $P_{N}(A) \sim e^{-N^{1/3} F((A-\left\langle A\right\rangle) / N^{2/3})}$. The large-deviation function $F(y)$ has a universal form for the three maps, differing only in the scaling constants. At a critical value $y=y_c$, it exhibits a corner singularity which has the character of a condensation transition. The transition separates between a subcritical phase $0< y<y_c$ in which the fluctuations are Gaussian and arise homogeneously from all of the $x_i$'s, and a supercritical phase $y>y_c$ in which a small fraction of the $x_i$'s give a macroscopic contribution to the fluctuation. Despite this anomalous behavior of the right tail, we find that the cumulants of the distribution $P_N(A)$ grow linearly with $N$ at large $N$, and calculate the associated coefficients.
authors: Lucianno Defaveri, Naftali R. Smith

papers.title: Asymptotics of the Moduli Spaces of Parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb C)$-Higgs Bundles
papers.abstract: We study the large-scale geometry of the moduli spaces of stable strongly parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere for a family of parabolic weights. We glue the local Toda model metric to a decoupled metric obtained from the spectral line bundle, and perturb the resulting approximate metrics to harmonic metrics adapted to the parabolic structure. We also prove that Hitchin's $L^2$ metric approaches the semi-flat metric exponentially. The metric comparison and the spectral period calculation show that each moduli space is a complete ALG gravitational instanton of type $E_6$. The asymptotic estimates are uniform on compact subintervals of the weight chamber.
authors: Shiyu Cao

papers.title: Critical Ising Model on the Periodic Cubic Lattice $(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^{3}$
papers.abstract: We investigate the critical behaviour of the nearest-neighbour Ising model on the three-dimensional periodic cubic lattice $(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^{3}$, and we present a companion set of Monte Carlo simulations. After recalling the rigorous results on the continuity of the spontaneous magnetization in $d=3$ and the triviality of the scaling limit in $d\ge 4$, we compile modern high-precision estimates of the 3D Ising critical exponents and verify the scaling relations that connect them. We then describe numerical measurements of the Binder cumulant, the magnetic susceptibility, the specific heat, the two-point correlation function, and the finite-size scaling of the magnetization. We discuss the systematic uncertainties that affect the extraction of the exponent ratios $\gamma/\nu$ and $\alpha/\nu$, and we emphasize that an exponential fit of the correlation function is not appropriate at the critical point, where the decay is algebraic.
authors: Shenglan Yuan

papers.title: Stitched surface codes: planar concatenation through GHZ corridors
papers.abstract: We present a fault-tolerant quantum-memory architecture that concatenates four distance-t rotated surface-code patches with the [[4,2,2]] outer code, encoding two logical qubits at code distance d = 2t in a physical footprint of N < 2(2t+1)^2 qubits on a square lattice with nearest-neighbor connectivity. The outer-code stabilizer generators XXXX and ZZZZ, each of physical weight 4t, are measured in situ via verified Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) ancillae distributed through narrow corridors between adjacent patches, without lattice surgery or long-range gates. The outer-code gadgets introduce hyperedge fault mechanisms, but by design each decomposes into graphlike components, so the complete syndrome is decoded by a single minimum-weight-perfect-matching pass. Circuit-level simulations show logical error rates that scale as p^t, consistent with distance-2t protection. Finally, we implement the construction experimentally on a 105-qubit Willow superconducting processor in both the ZZ and XX memory bases. With the correlated-matching decoder, increasing the code distance from d = 4 to d = 6 reduces the block logical error rate by a factor of 1.52. The construction thus provides a near-term testbed for concatenated architectures beyond the standard surface code.
authors: Mohamed A. Shalby, Alexandre Bourassa, Amir Karamlou, Leigh Martin, Alexis Morvan, Nicholas Noll, Craig Gidney, Leonid P. Pryadko

papers.title: Anti-successors and anti-replicators, Manin products and Koszul duality
papers.abstract: We develop an operadic theory of anti-splitting and anti-replication for binary operads. For a binary operad $\opd$, we define its anti-bisuccessor $\ABSu(\opd)$ and anti-trisuccessor $\ATSu(\opd)$, with the property that an operation of $\opd$ splits into a negative sum of two or three operations, yielding canonical operad morphisms $\opd \to\ABSu(\opd)$ and $\opd\to\ATSu(\opd)$. For binary quadratic operads, the process gives Manin black products, \[ \ABSu(\opd) \cong \antiprelie \bullet \opd, \qquad \ATSu(\opd)\cong \antipostlie\bullet\opd. \] Dually, we introduce the anti-duplicator \(\ADup(\mathcal P)\) and anti-triplicator \(\ATrip(\mathcal P)\) and prove \[ \ADup(\opd^!)\cong \ABSu(\opd)^!, \qquad \ATrip(\opd^!)\cong \ATSu(\opd)^!. \] Consequently, the anti-duplicator gives a new way to calculate Manin white products. %, in particular, $\ADup(\opd)\cong \antiperm\circ\opd$. The framework recovers known anti-splittings, including anti-dendriform, anti-pre-Lie, and anti-pre-Poisson structures, in a uniform operadic form and produces further examples and dual pairs.
authors: Chengming Bai, Li Guo, Yunhe Sheng, You Wang

papers.title: When do quantum views help? Complementary classical-quantum representations in multi-view fusion
papers.abstract: Recent studies have reported promising results from quantum machine learning in drug discovery, healthcare, materials science and cybersecurity. Research includes comparisons with classical machine learning algorithms and the development of sequential hybrid pipelines. We propose that fusion can improve prediction when classical and quantum representations capture complementary predictive relationships. Our classical-quantum multi-view framework preserves the full classical input alongside simulated quantum features. Concatenation and attention combine the views; single-view comparisons, replacement and masking controls assess both views' contributions. Controlled angular-polynomial experiments distinguish targets adequately represented by a single view from those that depend on complementary angular and polynomial relationships. For these mixed targets, fusion improves prediction by combining the relevant feature sets, while matched classical representations recover the same benefit, linking the improvement to their complementary predictive content. Controlled classification tests further show that gains depend on alignment between the chosen representation and the target, and on a suitable fusion rule. Benchmark validation shows improved mean predictive performance over classical baselines on Wine, Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer, three-class Fashion-MNIST and Steel Plates Faults within the evaluated protocols. Classical replacement and masking controls remain competitive, classical baselines lead on Digits and Covertype, and outcomes with missing or corrupted views depend on the available inputs. These findings support evaluating quantum representations for their complementary predictive contribution and matching the representation and fusion strategy to the target relationships.
authors: Azadeh Alavi, Fatemeh Kouchmeshki, Hossein Akhoundi, Yongli Re, Abdolrahman Alavi, Muhammad Usman

papers.title: Parallel Repetition for Entangled Games via Conditional Relative Entropy
papers.abstract: We give a proof of the cubic parallel-repetition bound for finite two-player entangled games using quantum conditional relative entropy. For a game with entangled value $1-\varepsilon<1$ and answer alphabets $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$, its $n$-fold repeated value is at most \[ \exp[-\Omega(\varepsilon^3n/L)],\qquad L:=\max\{1,\log(|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|)\}, \] for every $n\ge1$. This recovers Song's cubic rate. We also prove a threshold bound: the probability of winning a fraction at least $1-\varepsilon+\delta$ is at most $\exp[-\Omega(\delta^5n/(\varepsilon^2L))]$ for $0<\delta\le\varepsilon$. Our information charge is the decrease in relative entropy when a question reference is discarded. Our comparison states preserve the original conditional question law. A chain rule bounds the coordinate charges using the cost of conditioning on checked wins and retaining checked answers. Our main lemma converts small charges into nearby pure-state descriptions and local corrections, each depending only on one player's question. Together with Song's sampler, these enable approximate local preparation of the conditioned workspace.
authors: Rahul Jain

papers.title: Half-space last passage percolation with inhomogeneous first row
papers.abstract: We consider exponential last passage percolation in half-space with a deterministic first row. This model corresponds to a version of TASEP in half-space in which particles enter at the origin and are restricted by a moving wall. We determine the possible limiting distributions of rescaled last passage times depending on the boundary strength and the choice of the wall. As key inputs to our analysis, we establish several results for point-to-point half-space last passage times, including upper tail bounds, weak convergence, and bounds on the probabilities that geodesics touch the diagonal for certain start and end points.
authors: Patrik L. Ferrari, Sabrina Gernholt

papers.title: Optimising multipartite entanglement manipulation in quantum networks
papers.abstract: Long-range, genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) between distant parties in a quantum network is a crucial resource for distributed quantum information processing. Through controlled manipulation of short-range GME states in the network via stochastic local operations aided by classical communication (SLOCC), long-range GME can be established between selected target nodes on demand. Optimizing such multipartite entanglement distribution protocols under constraints imposed by the network architecture, target-node set, and available resource budget is a key challenge in resource-efficient manipulation of GME. We present a general operational framework for manipulating GME in quantum networks by classifying the relevant networking operations into three broad primitives-inflation, deflation, and purification-reflecting their effect on the proliferation of GME through general bounds and illustrative examples. We show how these primitives can be combined to construct a broad class of multipartite quantum repeater protocols, enabling their systematic optimization, and demonstrate the framework with a simple example. Applying our approach to networks of D\"ur-Cirac-Tarrach states reveals a rich landscape of achievable end-to-end GME and accessible entanglement classes. More generally, our framework provides a systematic approach to the construction and optimization of multipartite quantum repeater protocols for scalable and resource-efficient GME distribution in quantum networks.
authors: Shashank Shekhar, David Elkouss, Siddhartha Santra

papers.title: Bound States Inside the Horizon and Black Hole Entropy
papers.abstract: We study the bound states perturbations in the interior of the Schwarzschild black hole and examine whether or not their microstates spectrum can furnish a statistical description of the black hole entropy. These states contain a discrete set of modes characterized by the labels $(s, p,\ell,m)$, where $s$ represents the spin of the species, $p$ denotes the radial excitation number while $(\ell,m)$ are the usual angular momentum labels. Requiring that the shortest wavelength resolved by the highly excited bound states remains above the quantum gravity scale introduces an angular cutoff $\ell_{\rm max}\sim r_H/L_{\rm Pl}$. The resulting angular degeneracy therefore scales with the horizon area. We count the corresponding configurations in the microcanonical ensemble and find an entropy of the form $S_{\rm bs}=\alpha A/\hbar G$. Demanding that the bound state sector to be in thermal equilibrium with the black hole at the Hawking temperature fixes the fraction of the bound state energy in total black hole energy. For the gravitational perturbations sector, the equilibrium bound state contribution in entropy and the energy fraction are typically small. We also examine the conditions under which the bound states could account for the full black hole entropy. Although such saturation is possible at the level of state counting, it requires an order unity fraction in the black hole energy and therefore the backreactions on the background geometry cannot be ignored.
authors: Hassan Firouzjahi

papers.title: Crossovers between Time-Bin and Energy-Time Entanglement in Homodyned Resonance Fluorescence
papers.abstract: We theoretically investigate photonic entanglement generated by homodyning resonance fluorescence from a two-level emitter with a phase-locked laser field. Under weak excitation, increasing the relative laser-field amplitude produces crossovers from time-bin to energy--time and back to time-bin entanglement. The intermediate energy--time regime occurs near amplitude matching, where destructive interference suppresses the single-photon component, allowing the two-photon contributions to dominate the coincidence signal. We evaluate the resulting photon statistics and first-order coherence and characterize the entanglement through violations of the CHSH Bell inequality in a Franson interferometer. This scheme provides a route to controlling photonic entanglement through linear optics and coherent interference.
authors: Zi-Qi Zeng, Jian Wang, Bang Wu, Zhiliang Yuan

papers.title: Strict unimodality of the exact time-domain diffuse-light response under a Robin boundary condition
papers.abstract: Time-domain boundary measurements of diffuse light are temporal point-spread functions whose peak position is used as a robust scalar datum in diffuse optical and fluorescence imaging. We consider the exact response generated by a single fluorescent point target in a homogeneous half-space with a Robin boundary condition. The response is a temporal convolution of two diffusion Green-function factors containing a complementary-error-function boundary correction. For every positive diffusion, absorption, depth, and source--target and detector--target distance parameter, and for every nonnegative Robin parameter, we prove that the normalized exact response is a generalized gamma convolution density. Its extension by zero to the negative half-line is bell-shaped. A differentiable small-time expansion, established by sectorial analyticity and Cauchy estimates, together with the sign-change structure of the first two derivatives, excludes tangential critical points and yields a unique peak with strict increase before it and strict decrease after it. The argument is exact and requires no large-distance, source--detector balance, symmetry, restricted-time, or small-parameter assumption. The same conclusion holds after convolution with an exponential fluorescence-lifetime density for every positive lifetime. The key ingredients are an explicit Stieltjes representation of the Robin factor, hyperbolic complete monotonicity, closure of the generalized gamma convolution class, and bell-shape theory. A derivation of the exact half-space model and the differentiated endpoint asymptotics are included in two appendices.
authors: Junyong Eom, Jinwan Park

papers.title: Accurate gap control of 3D-integrated superconducting quantum circuits using asymmetric indium architecture and multi-angle flip-chip bonding
papers.abstract: Flip-chip 3D integration is a key enabling technology for overcoming the routing and layout constraints of planar superconducting quantum processors, but it requires accurate and uniform control of the inter-chip spacing while preserving qubit coherence. In conventional processes, thick indium bumps are deposited symmetrically on both chips, while dedicated spacers are introduced to limit the residual tilt. Here, we present a flip-chip bonding process based on an asymmetric indium architecture, combining $20\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ thick indium bumps on the control chip with $200\,\mathrm{nm}$ thin indium pads on the qubit chip. Using electrical and microwave measurements, we demonstrate low resistance and low loss indium interconnects, and show that transmon qubits integrated with this process reach relaxation and coherence times of $T_1=(159\pm14)\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ and $T_{\mathrm{2,echo}}=(294\pm42)\,\mu\mathrm{s}$, respectively, comparable to planar devices. Combined with a multi angle compression procedure that suppresses systematic tilt, this approach reduces the average post bonding tilt to $(20\pm12)\,\mu\mathrm{rad}$. These results establish an asymmetric indium architecture combined with multi angle compression as a robust, coherence preserving route toward 3D integrated superconducting quantum processors.
authors: L. Richard, N. Bruckmoser, J. Feigl, D. Bunch, A. Bhattacharjee, L. Koch, I. Tsitsilin, V. P. Bader, H. Hu, L. S\"odergren, S. Filipp

papers.title: Casimir forces on suspended thin dielectric membranes covered with graphene
papers.abstract: We investigate the Casimir force on thin suspended dielectric layers covered with graphene, both theoretically and experimentally. Thermal effects of the Casimir force on graphene occur at separations significantly smaller compared to ordinary metals and dielectrics. At such small separations, the Casimir force is sufficiently strong to be measured experimentally. However, the presence of substrates to support the graphene significantly reduces the enhancement. We show theoretically that replacing the solid substrate beneath graphene with a thin dielectric membrane partially restores this strong thermal dependence. One of the interacting objects is a solid gold plate. The other object is a suspended dielectric membrane made of either 15 nm of silicon oxide or 13 nm silicon nitride, covered with graphene. At a separation of $\sim$500 nm, theoretical predictions yield changes in the Casimir pressure of up to 54 % and 40 % for silicon oxide and silicon nitride, respectively, when the temperature is increased from 10 K to 294 K. Measurements were performed for graphene on a suspended silicon nitride membrane at room temperature, using a gold-coated sphere attached to a cantilever as the force sensor. The measured force gradient is consistent with the theoretical prediction, although the thermal dependence could not be resolved, in part because of uncertainties in the optical properties of silicon nitride. Replacing a bulk substrate with a thin dielectric membrane covered with graphene provides a substantial reduction of the Casimir force, which may facilitate the stable operation of neutral nanomechanical elements at small separations.
authors: Tze Ue Ngai, Zuocheng Zhang, Q. Zhang, Youssef Jeyar, Jingwei Li, Zhengtang Luo, Mauro Antezza, H. B. Chan

papers.title: Semiclassical Band Splitting in the Infinite Chern Band Model
papers.abstract: We study the two lowest Bloch bands of the infinite Chern band model in the semiclassical limit. When the Berry curvature parameter is an odd multiple of \(\pi\), we derive an explicit asymptotic formula for their exponentially small splitting, uniformly over the Brillouin torus. The proof combines Agmon estimates and WKB approximations for a matrix Schr\"odinger operator whose lowest potential eigenvalue has two wells. Geometric properties of the Agmon distance allow us to compute the leading tunneling coefficients by the method of stationary phase. We provide numerical computations to illustrate the asymptotic formula and support the conjecture that the two bands remain separated for other values of the Berry curvature parameter.
authors: Tyler Guo

papers.title: Periodic conditional measurements on a photonic chip
papers.abstract: Quantum measurements not only extract information but also reshape quantum evolution through measurement backaction. Here, we investigate periodic conditional measurements, in which coherent evolution is repeatedly interrupted by local measurements. We show that the bright and dark modes of the conditional evolution operator provide a unified spectral description of both the post-selected final state along no-detection trajectories and the statistics of detection events. Using a three-dimensional photonic chip, we demonstrate on-demand state engineering through dark-mode preservation and bright-mode selection, enabling the protection of topological corner states and excited-state shelving. We further observe the predicted transition of the total detection probability on an effectively infinite one-dimensional lattice and identify its microscopic origin in Floquet near-dark modes. These results establish periodic conditional measurements as a general framework for engineering conditional quantum states and manipulating event-detection statistics in monitored quantum dynamics.
authors: Xuan Chen, Ruo-Yu Yin, Xiao-Wen Shang, Xi-Jun Yuan, Ze-Feng Lan, Hong-Jing Du, Yi-Jun Chang, Bao-Jing Liu, Wen-Hao Zhou, Xi Tan, Eli Barkai, Hao Tang, Xian-Min Jin

papers.title: Limits of adaptive linear postprocessing in six-state quantum key distribution
papers.abstract: Two-way classical communication improves the noise tolerance of quantum key distribution, but the limits of adaptive parity processing remain unclear. For the six-state protocol with equal three-basis error rate $p\in[p_*,1/2]$, where $p_*=(5-\sqrt5)/10\simeq27.64\%$, we construct a single compatible collective attack that defeats a broad class of linear postprocessing. Each public message may be an affine function of the sender's raw key, chosen adaptively from the public history. For every finite input length and every accepted transcript of positive probability, Eve's optimal probability of recovering any affine function of Alice's raw key is at least Bob's. Consequently, reliable agreement on a linear final key is incompatible with secrecy. The same conclusion holds for arbitrary publicly seeded privacy amplification after reliable recovery of a linear candidate. The proof conditions on the complete transcript, which restricts the two raw keys to affine subspaces. A local degradation of Eve's state, a known R\'enyi-entropy comparison, and a coset-probability inequality then give the recovery comparison. Both inequalities are proved in self-contained appendices. The result allows block splitting, regrouping, nonzero-syndrome selection, and adaptive linear reconciliation.
authors: Toyohiro Tsurumaru

papers.title: Approach to Equilibrium in Translation-Invariant Quantum Systems: Structural Results II
papers.abstract: We continue the development, started in [AHP 25 (2023), 715-749], of a structural theory of approach to equilibrium in translation-invariant quantum spin systems. Dynamical Steady States (DSS) are defined as w*-limit points of the time-averaged evolution of an initial state. We show that if a DSS is an equilibrium state of a sufficiently regular interaction, then the specific energy of this interaction is necessarily a constant of the motion. Two distinct mechanisms lead to this conclusion, one based on dynamical surface energies and the other on conservation of specific relative entropy. We conjecture that these properties hold for a natural class of interactions. For a DSS admitting a physical equilibrium description, the associated equilibrium states are characterized by a dynamical Gibbs variational principle: they are precisely the minimizers of the specific relative entropy from the initial state over the physical equilibrium states. The achieved minimum equals the increase of specific entropy. The structural theory also yields characterizations of approach to thermal equilibrium, based on two model-dependent questions: restoration of a sufficiently local thermodynamic description at large times and classification of the corresponding local constants of motion. Once locality is restored, the constants of motion determine the possible asymptotic equilibrium states. In particular, if finite-range locality is restored and the energy is the only finite-range constant of the motion, then every DSS is a thermal equilibrium state at the temperature fixed by energy conservation. The finite-time dynamical input underlying this theory is established in a companion paper.
authors: Vojkan Jak\v{s}i\'c, Claude-Alain Pillet, Anna Szczepanek

papers.title: Difference between pair creation and anomaly matching: Nontrivial aspects of invertible symmetries and defects in $SU(N)$ models
papers.abstract: We study the connection between the $SU(N)_{K}$ Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) model and $SU(N)_{K'}$ WZW models, enforcing the unbroken $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ symmetries. The fundamental underlying structures are the (half-)integer spin simple currents in the topological quantum field theories and anomaly matching conditions in conformal field theories. For the (half-)integer spin simple current condition of the folded models $SU(N)_{K}\boxtimes_{\mathbb{Z}_{N}} \overline{SU(N)_{K'}}$ or $SU(N)_{K}\boxtimes_{\mathbb{Z}_{N}} SU(N)_{K'}$, we obtain the generalized pairing condition $K= \pm R^{2}K' (\text{mod}.N)$ with $\text{gcd}(R,N)=1$. On the other hand, the anomaly matching condition results in the weaker condition $K= \pm RUK' (\text{mod}.N)$ with $\text{gcd}(R,N)=\text{gcd}(U,N)=1$. Surprisingly, the anomaly matching without the pairing condition results in the intrinsic mismatch of the preservation law of the $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ defects and symmetries. The pairing condition canonically relates symmetries and defects, as in category theory, whereas it is unclear whether it can be a guiding principle in prohibiting the massless renormalization group flows.
authors: Yoshiki Fukusumi, Shuma Nakashiba

papers.title: Dynamical Conservation Laws in Quantum Spin Systems
papers.abstract: We study dynamical conservation laws and the propagation of thermodynamic structure in translation-invariant lattice quantum spin systems. Using Lieb-Robinson bounds [CMP 28 (1972), 251-257] in arbitrary dimension, and Araki's bounds [CMP 14 (1969), 120-157] in dimension one, we prove conservation of the specific entropy, specific energy, and specific relative entropy under suitable assumptions on the interactions. The transported local Hamiltonians admit surface energies that vanish per unit volume in the van Hove limit, and local observables remain a core for the transported generators at every finite time. Weak Gibbsianity is preserved for sufficiently small times in arbitrary dimension and for all times in dimension one. These results provide the analytical foundation for the structural theory of approach to equilibrium developed in a companion paper, and establish partial results toward the conjectures formulated there.
authors: Vojkan Jak\v{s}i\'c, Claude-Alain Pillet, Anna Szczepanek

papers.title: Finite-Frequency Boson-Number Bounds Across the Quantum Rabi Transition
papers.abstract: We consider the quantum Rabi model, a fundamental model of quantum optics describing a two-level system coupled to a bosonic mode, including counter-rotating terms. In the limit of large separation between the two-level transition frequency and the bosonic mode frequency, the model exhibits a quantum phase transition at a critical coupling strength. Although the model is exactly solvable, simple analytic expressions for important physical quantities are generally unavailable. We derive rigorous upper and lower bounds for the ground-state energy and boson occupation number across the quantum phase transition at finite frequency ratios. Our results characterize the subcritical, critical, and supercritical regimes and establish the scaling behavior of the boson occupation near the critical point. Exact numerical diagonalization demonstrates the tightness of the derived bounds, while the resulting finite-frequency inequalities provide experimentally testable predictions for trapped-ion quantum simulators.
authors: Razmik G. Unanyan, Michael Fleischhauer, Nikolay V. Vitanov

papers.title: Reducing the Cost of Qudit State Preparation by Learning a Sparse Structure for SNAP Gates
papers.abstract: Preparing quantum states in bosonic qudits with SNAP--Displacement sequences requires both optimizing the gate parameters and deciding which Fock levels should be controlled by each SNAP gate. A fully parameterized ansatz assigns an independent phase to every Fock level in every gate, leading to a number of phases that grows steeply. This constitutes a problem for short to medium term systems as controlling many phases requires complex control pulses which are subject to increased control errors. Previous work reduced this cost by restricting the trainable phases to predefined sparse patterns, such as a diagonal or a grid, which however may not be optimal for a specific target state. In this work, we address this limitation by introducing a method that learns which phases are needed together with their values, using a differentiable mask. A sparsity penalty encourages the removal of unnecessary phases, while temperature annealing gradually turns the masks into binary decisions. We compare the proposed method with fully parameterized and predefined sparse ansatzes on Fourier and Haar-random target states. The evaluation considers both the minimum number of phases required to reach different infidelity thresholds and the overall trade-off between fidelity and phases required, measured through Pareto frontiers and hypervolume. The results show that learning the location of the phases together with their values provides competitive or improved fidelity--resource trade-offs, although the advantage depends on the target state and qudit dimension.
authors: Marco Pennazio, Leonardo Ignazio Pagliochini, Riccardo Pellini, Maurizio Ferrari Dacrema, Paolo Cremonesi

papers.title: Krylov complexity and oscillatory quantum dynamics in two-field inflation
papers.abstract: We investigate Krylov-space dynamics of primordial perturbations in two-field inflation. Starting from the quadratic action for coupled curvature and entropy perturbations, we solve the mode equations with Bunch-Davies initial conditions and construct the corresponding quadratic Hamiltonian. The Gaussian quantum state is described by a four-mode squeezed state with two squeezing channels. We derive the evolution of the squeezing strength and squeezing angle and use them to evaluate the Krylov complexity, Krylov entropy, and channel-resolved Lanczos coefficients. Our numerical results show that the two channels remain weakly squeezed inside the horizon but develop different squeezing histories after horizon exit. The two channels exhibit different onset times and distinct oscillatory Krylov dynamics. The second channel develops strong squeezing earlier and dominates the intermediate evolution, whereas the first channel shows a delayed enhancement. The corresponding Krylov complexities exhibit oscillatory structures across horizon crossing and pronounced fluctuations in the strongly squeezed superhorizon regime. These oscillations originate from the relative phases entering the squeezing equations and are amplified through the nonlinear relation between Krylov complexity of different channels.
authors: Tao Li, Lei-Hua Liu, Hai-Bing Fu

papers.title: Augmentation curve for torus knots
papers.abstract: We prove a version of topological recursion for the correlation differentials of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials of torus knots on the corresponding augmentation curves, following the proposal of Gu, Jockers, Klemm, and Soroush. To this end, we explicitly construct the spectral curve from the so-called auxiliary curve of Brini, Eynard, and Mari\~no and prove that it coincides with the augmentation curve for every torus knot with coprime $(r,s)$. Finally, our version of topological recursion proves the higher-genus closed-string prediction of the Aganagic--Vafa conjecture for all torus knot augmentation curves.
authors: Alexander Hock, Sergey Shadrin

papers.title: Fortuitous BMN Cohomology at Every $N$
papers.abstract: Finite-$N$ trace relations can produce $Q$-cohomology classes with no stable large-$N$ ancestor. The brane-fused construction at $SU(3)$ suggests that such states can retain an $SU(2)$ nonabelian core accompanied by scalar hair. We develop this idea into a general construction for every $SU(N)$, $N\geq3$. Starting from the $SU(2)$ threshold operator $O_{24}$, we select pairs of eigenvalues of one scalar and construct corrected two-colour letters whose $Q$-transformations obey the $SU(2)$ rules exactly. Substitution into $O_{24}$ gives a closed rational operator for each pair. Multiplying by eigenvalue-separation factors removes the denominators, and summing over all pairs produces a gauge-invariant polynomial. An exact block-restriction identity recovers a nonzero multiple of $O_{24}$. The restriction maps every stable class to a stable $SU(2)$ class, proving that the resulting operator is non-exact and fortuitous, even when non-Coulombic stable classes are included. This proves the existence of fortuitous BMN cohomology at every $N\geq3$. The construction is an exact algebraic realization of a nonabelian core with scalar dressing.
authors: Robert de Mello Koch, Minkyoo Kim, Sinong Liu

papers.title: Time-optimal robust quantum control for partially known errors
papers.abstract: Robust quantum control usually assumes one of two extremes: the error is of a known form and only its strength is unknown, or nothing at all is known about it. In practice one often sits in between. The size of a static error is unknown, but its class is known, for example, it only shifts energy levels, or it acts on each subsystem separately. We ask how fast a control can cancel, to first order, every error in such a class. A time-independent Hamiltonian can do this if and only if all errors in the class have zero diagonal in a common basis. In that case an equally spaced energy ladder in this basis does it after one period. A lower bound that holds for any time-dependent control with bounded drive power shows that this simple constant control is optimal for several natural classes, including unknown level shifts and unknown local errors on two subsystems. Completely unknown errors need a time-dependent control, and there, knowing the error class shortens the minimum time by a factor $\sqrt{d^2+1}$. So partial knowledge of the error changes not only how long an optimal robust control takes, but also its form.
authors: Lloren\c{c} Balada Gaggioli

papers.title: Practical Fidelity Estimation for Noisy Quantum Devices Using Direct and Survival-Probability-Based Protocols
papers.abstract: Reliable characterization of quantum states and quantum processes is central to the development of scalable quantum computing. Standard characterization techniques such as full quantum state tomography become rapidly impractical as system size increases. In this work we present two software-oriented fidelity estimation protocols that avoid full tomographic reconstruction while remaining experimentally relevant for noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices. The first protocol is direct fidelity estimation (DFE), where the fidelity between a target state and an experimentally prepared state is estimated from importance-sampled Pauli measurements. The second protocol is a survival-probability-based method that reconstructs fidelity from experimentally accessible moments of a noisy evolution and its approximate inverse, and is intrinsically robust against state-preparation-and-measurement (SPAM) errors. We discuss the theoretical basis of both approaches, analyze their noise sensitivity, and present numerical evidence on representative multiqubit states under depolarizing, dephasing, and amplitude-damping channels. For DFE we show that attenuation-aware correction improves robustness against measurement noise. For the survival-probability approach we show that an $L_2$-optimized expansion substantially outperforms naive Taylor truncation in high-noise regimes.
authors: Ahmed Aman, Kaustav Chatterjee, Younes Javanmard, Tanmoy Pandit

papers.title: Driving the cooling process of a quantum system via classical noise
papers.abstract: It is known that under particular hypotheses anomalous thermalization processes can occur, such as the Mpemba effect, consisting in a faster cooling down when the system is prepared in a hotter initial condition, thus making convenient to warm up the system before the freezing process in order to make it freeze in a shorter time. It is shown here that the action of a Markovian classical noise during the freezing process can accelerate the approach to the zero-temperature thermal state. This prediction is counterintuitive, especially after observing that a classical noise can be considered equivalent to the action of an infinite-temperature reservoir, since both drive the system toward the same state. These facts lead to the statement that warming up the system during the contact with a low-temperature reservoir can accelerate the cooling process.
authors: B. Militello, A. Napoli

papers.title: Fast, parallel, three-dimensional rearrangement of atom arrays using superpositions of elementary holograms
papers.abstract: Assembling defect-free arrays of neutral atoms requires real-time rearrangement of stochastically loaded optical tweezers. Conventional rearrangement methods shuttle atoms sequentially, whereas high-speed spatial light modulators (SLMs) can move all atoms in parallel, which scales more favorably as the array size grows. For fast parallel rearrangement, the sequence of holograms displayed on the SLM should be computed more rapidly than the SLM refresh rate, and there should be phase continuity between successive holograms to minimize transient intensity fluctuations. We calculate holograms analytically by adding together the complex fields needed to produce each individual trap, and we ramp the phase of each trap linearly as it moves to its target location. Trap positions enter as continuous variables, rather than tied to points on a grid, so the method provides high positioning accuracy. Using a single GPU, we compute each intermediate hologram in 0.284 ms, considerably faster than the SLM refresh time of 0.696 ms, so the rearrangement speed is hardware-limited. In each step, we use the free processing time to iteratively optimize the holograms for equal intensity across the traps, decreasing trap non-uniformity to 1.24% during rearrangement at no cost in total time. Starting from an array of 256 sites loaded stochastically with $^{87}$Rb atoms, we assemble a 100-atom array in under 20 ms with a rearrangement survival probability of 99.31(12)% per atom. This rearrangement increases the temperature of the atoms by 9(3) $\mu$K, which is small compared to the trap depth of 480 $\mu$K. Our method can also move individual atoms axially, enabling transport in different planes. We demonstrate this capability with a rearrangement protocol where one set of atoms leapfrogs over another.
authors: D. J. Hoare, P. Dunniece, J. Rodewald, K. K. Voges, M. R. Tarbutt

papers.title: Statistical Characterization of Erratic and Chaotic Processes through Their Extrema I. Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We propose a general statistical framework for characterizing erratic functions through the statistics of their extrema, with the aim of identifying statistical signatures associated with chaotic processes. It is based on analyzing the extrema points of erratic functions associated with these processes. One is instructed to determine the probability distribution functions ( PDF)s of the locations of the extrema points, the spacings between the locations, in particular the nearest neighbors, and the ratios between adjacent spacings. We then fit these PDFs with PDFs known to relate to chaotic behavior like of random matrix theory. The extrema considered establish a cloud of points in general in $D$ dimensions for erratic function of several variables. For certain systems one finds also extrema curves. We further determine the ``thermodynamic" description of the erratic functions by computing the Shannon or differential entropy and by equating the PDFs to the Gibbs one. With this map we determine the ``energy function" and for certain cases also the ``temperature". We analyze three benchmark spacing PDFs: the Bernoulli shift map, the Poisson and the Gaussian beta ensemble and several others. We want to emphasize that the map to thermodynamics can be applied to variety of chaotic processes including non-physics ones. We distinguish marginal spacing distributions from joint distributions of consecutive spacings. The latter probe correlations and statistical organization that are invisible in one-spacing PDFs and may provide stronger signatures for distinguishing structured chaotic-like behavior from uncorrelated irregularity.
authors: Jacob Sonnenschein

papers.title: Degree Growth of Rational Maps with Laurent Property
papers.abstract: Algebraic entropy measures the exponential growth of the degrees of iterates of rational self-maps. It is introduced by Bellon and Viallet in \cite{BellonandViallet}. We study degree growth for rational maps arising from recurrences with the Laurent property, with particular emphasis on Gale--Robinson recurrences. We develop a direct method for determining the degree growth from the recurrence relation itself, reducing the problem to the study of associated max-linear, or tropical recurrences. We first obtain a closed formula for the degrees of iterates for a broad class of homogeneous quadratic Laurent recurrences. We then apply this result to the two-term Gale--Robinson family and derive an explicit quadratic growth formula with a periodic correction term. For three-term Gale--Robinson recurrences, we express the algebraic entropy in terms of the associated tropical growth rate sequence. Based on explicit computations, we formulate a conjecture for the general three-term family predicting quadratic growth with a periodic correction. We prove the conjecture for the infinite family with parameters $p=1$, $q=2$, and $r\geq3$.
authors: Melih Emin Can

papers.title: Finite-size geometric crossover toward fragmentation of the potential energy shell in the quantum random energy model
papers.abstract: The quantum random energy model (QREM) is a paradigmatic model for studying delocalization-localization transitions at finite energy density in Fock space. In the computational basis, its diagonal energies are independent Gaussian random variables, in contrast to the correlated energies of local interacting models such as the disordered XXZ chain. In this work, we construct a potential energy shell associated with a basis state, defined through its energy variance, and investigate its connectivity on the Fock-space hypercube. As the transverse field is varied, this energy-selected subgraph undergoes a finite-size geometric crossover between fully connected and fragmented regimes. Furthermore, we observe a correlation between the shell connectivity and the finite-size fractal dimension of the eigenstates, as extracted from the participation entropy. For the QREM, the statistical independence of the diagonal energies allows the shell connectivity to be analyzed as an effective independent site percolation problem on the hypercube, with its crossover scale estimated within a one-hop approximation. At finite energy density, this estimate gives a nonmonotonic dependence of the crossover scale on system size $L$: increasing $L$ initially favors connectivity, while beyond an energy-dependent scale $L^*(\varepsilon)$ the trend reverses towards fragmentation.
authors: Ishita Modak, Vatsana Tiwari, Soumya Bera

papers.title: Distribution Functions and Moments of Harmonically Trapped Inertial Run-and-Tumble Particles in a Shear-Thickening Medium
papers.abstract: We study the dynamics of an athermal inertial active particle confined in a harmonic potential and moving through shear-thickening media in one dimension. The activity is modeled using a symmetric dichotomous noise of strength $\Sigma$ and flipping rate $\lambda$, which mimics a run-and-tumble particle. The shear-thickening response of the medium is incorporated through a velocity-dependent viscous force of the form $g(v) \sim \tan(v)$. Starting from the Fokker-Planck equations corresponding to the particle's dynamics, we numerically compute the time-dependent joint probability density function $f(x,v,t)$ using a finite-volume upwind scheme. Next, we numerically solve the particle's equations of motion to obtain the steady-state position $P_s(x)$ and velocity $W_s(v)$ distributions and compare them with the marginal distributions obtained from $f(x,v,t)$ at sufficiently large $t$. The two approaches show excellent agreement. Both $P_s(x)$ and $W_s(v)$ exhibit several intriguing transitions as $\lambda$ is varied, and they eventually approach Gaussian-like profiles at sufficiently large $\lambda$. Our study of the time-dependent position-velocity correlation, $\langle xv \rangle(t)$, shows that larger values of $\lambda$ lead to faster relaxation to the steady state when all other parameters are held constant.
authors: Subhanker Howlader, Prasenjit Das

papers.title: Theory of Dispersion and Exchange Interactions Subjected to Surface Roughness in Application to Signal Transmission through a Nanoswitch
papers.abstract: We present the theoretical description of a resistive nanoswitch designated for a change-over between the two operation modes by calculating the electri elastic, dispersion (van der Waals and Casimir), and also exchange repulsive forces in its configuration with an account of surface roughness. The dispersion forces are described by means of the Lifshitz theory and, at the shortest separations between the interacting bodies, where this theory is inapplicable, by the method of additive summation of the interatomic potentials corrected for the role of the effects of nonadditivity. The exchange repulsion is also found by a summation of the interatomic potentials and using the proximity force approximation. It is shown that the nanoswitch possesses the equilibrium closest separation between a cantilever tip and a ground plate calculated as a function of the actuation voltage and operates in a cyclic manner with no pull-in when this voltage is switched on and off. We have found the tunnel current between a cantilever tip and a plate and investigated distortions appearing in the signal transmitted through a nanoswitch. According to our results, the amplitude distortions arising in the low-frequency information signal can be made sufficiently small by increasing a difference between the amplitudes of the carrier and information signals. Possible applications of the obtained results are discussed.
authors: Galina L. Klimchitskaya, Alexander S. Korotkov, Vera V. Loboda, Vladimir M. Mostepanenko

papers.title: Diffusion Language Models as Open Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Diffusion language models generate text by reversing a classical diffusion process over token sequences. We show that their continuous-time forward and reverse dynamics can be embedded in the framework of open quantum systems, which describes quantum systems interacting with their environment. This connection provides a basis for extending diffusion sampling to superpositions of sentence states and for modifying the underlying generation dynamics. We construct a $\tau$-leaping unraveling scheme that simulates stochastic trajectories of these states while updating multiple token positions at each step. This enables generation conditioned on superposed prompts or thoughts, which we call Superposition of Prompts (SoP) and Superposition of Thoughts (SoT). The same formulation yields Quantum-Inspired Remasking (QIR): perturbing the masked-diffusion dynamics produces a confidence-based rule for revising previously generated tokens. Experiments with pretrained diffusion language models show that superposition-based generation can retain information from conditioning components not selected at the final measurement, while QIR improves LLM-assessed text quality when applied at an appropriate stage of generation.
authors: Akinori Tanaka, Yukinao Akamatsu, Takuki Tomita, Yuji Hirono

papers.title: Quantum instanton approach to metastable collective spin systems: Numerical implementation and applications
papers.abstract: Driven-dissipative collective spin systems can host several long-lived metastable states; rare switching between them governs slow relaxation and first-order dissipative phase transitions associated with changes in the dominant stationary state. In the companion Letter [arXiv:2604.15091], we introduced a quantum instanton framework based on exact quasiprobability dynamics to describe this switching and illustrated it with a minimal model possessing a simplifying symmetry. Here we develop its numerical implementation, combining collocation and shooting methods, and apply it to two microscopically motivated systems: the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model with purely collective dissipation and the cooperative resonance fluorescence with collective and local dissipation. By determining the leading exponential scaling of switching rates between metastable attractors, we predict the stationary magnetization, the first-order dissipative phase-transition point, and the exponential scaling of slow relaxation rates. These predictions agree with quantum master-equation calculations and an exact analytical result for the second model without dephasing. We also examine how the choice of quasiprobability representation affects numerical convergence and find that the alternative semiclassical Wigner approach, based on Gaussian truncation, has varying accuracy across models and parameter regimes. These results substantiate the framework's applicability to experimentally relevant collective spin systems with both collective and local dissipation.
authors: Maciej Chudak, Massimiliano Esposito, Krzysztof Ptaszynski

papers.title: Non-Invertible Froggatt-Nielsen Symmetry
papers.abstract: We investigate non-invertible completions of anomalous flavor symmetries and their application to Dirac neutrino masses. We formulate symmetry defects dressed by topological quantum field theories for flavor symmetries including finite non-Abelian flavor transformations with rational anomaly characters and modular flavor symmetries with the rational part of modular anomaly cocycles, for gauge sectors with the required exact higher-form symmetry. As a concrete example, we construct a Froggatt-Nielsen (FN) model in which an order-four subgroup $\mathbb Z_4^{\rm FN}\subset U(1)_{\rm FN}$ is completed into a non-invertible defect through its mixed anomaly with an intermediate hidden $U(1)_H$ gauge sector in the infrared monopole-decoupling limit. The non-invertible FN symmetry can be explicitly broken at the energy scale where monopoles become dynamical. This breaking from the infrared viewpoint can be realized in an ultraviolet hidden $SU(2)_H$ theory as instanton effects, where a constrained instanton with topological charge one generates a fermion mixing term that violates FN charge by one unit. Its coefficient contains the nonperturbative factor $\zeta_H\sim\exp[-8\pi^2/g_H^2(v_H)]$. When independent FN-breaking terms are subleading, integrating out the heavy fermions gives $(Y_\nu)_{ij}\propto\zeta_H\epsilon^{\ell_i+n_j}$ in a rotated basis for the right-handed neutrinos, to leading order in the instanton-induced fermion mixing. The nonperturbative factor provides the exponential suppression of the neutrino Yukawa couplings, while the FN charges determine the powers of $\epsilon$. For the chosen FN charges and generic order-one coefficients, $m_2/m_3\sim\epsilon$, favoring normal ordering. An independent $\mathbb Z_8^D$ gauge symmetry forbids Majorana masses. The same FN charge assignment reproduces the leading quark and charged-lepton Yukawa hierarchies.
authors: Hajime Otsuka, Ryo Yokokura

papers.title: An exact Simpson-Visser family in bumblebee gravity
papers.abstract: We construct an exact Simpson-Visser solution in metric bumblebee gravity, supported by a phantom scalar, magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics, and a spacelike configuration of fixed norm. The independent vector equation determines a local Lagrange multiplier and a temporal component that permits a regular ingoing extension across metric horizons. Reconstruction of the matter functions identifies a continuous family of wormholes, null minimum geometries, and black-bounces within one action. In the black hole case, the areal photon sphere and critical timelike orbit radii retain their Schwarzschild values, whereas angular deflection, periapsis advance, and photon orbit instability depend on the bounce and bumblebee parameters. The metric shadow coincides with the Schwarzschild prediction at fixed lapse mass and areal observer position; in addition, the adopted Sgr A* shadow diameter and M87* angular mass comparisons do not determine these parameters separately. The coupled axial equations yield distinct tensor, metric, and transverse bumblebee characteristics. We compute fundamental auxiliary massless scalar and ordinary Maxwell probe resonances by Chebyshev spectral collocation and estimate the tensor and bumblebee resonance scales at leading geometric optics order. Nonnegative probe potentials exclude exponentially growing probe modes. For negative nonminimal coupling and a nonzero temporal case, however, the supporting electromagnetic field develops an angular gradient instability in its extraordinary polarization. The unstable characteristic persists in the coupled principal symbol, while a variational construction establishes growing modes on the fixed geometry and lower bounds on their growth rates.
authors: A. A. Ara\'{u}jo Filho

papers.title: Renormalization of Quantum Gravity with Lagrange Multiplier Fields
papers.abstract: We study the renormalization of Einstein gravity coupled to a scalar field in the Lagrange multiplier (LM) formulation, where a pair of quantum LM fields, $(\lambda'_{\mu\nu},\sigma')$, is coupled to the gauge-fixed gravitational and scalar equations of motion. Using the fact that in this approach there are no higher loop corrections, we show that renormalizing the two quantum LM fields at one-loop order absorbs, off-shell, five out of the six independent divergent structures. The remaining off-shell counterterm, proportional to $ (\partial_\mu\bar\phi\,\partial^\mu\bar\phi)^2, $ is nonzero on shell and cannot be absorbed by any LM field redefinition, since such redefinitions generate only counterterms that vanish on shell. In contrast, in pure gravity (no matter), the LM renormalization absorbs all one-loop divergences and no additional counterterms are required. The LM formulation therefore provides a sharp off-shell separation between equation-of-motion divergences, absorbed into LM field renormalizations, and the single irreducible structure.
authors: F. T. Brandt, J. Frenkel, S. Martins-Filho, D. G. C. McKeon

papers.title: Correlation between normal character and Raman intensities of isotopologues of carbon dioxide
papers.abstract: Previous studies on the vibrational structure of carbon dioxide isotopologues have revealed a correlation between the strength of Fermi interactions and a recently defined normal-mode parameter. In this contribution, we investigate how the Raman intensities of the most intense bands evolve across the complete series of carbon dioxide isotopologues at room temperature. To this end, we introduce a general scheme for simulating Raman intensities in linear triatomic molecules, based on the computation of the mean polarizability surface up to cubic terms for all twelve stable species. For the first time, we establish correlations between the degree of normality and the Raman transition intensities, mean polarizability derivatives, and variational Raman shift errors across the CO$_2$ isotopologue series. The observed trends are further analyzed by considering rotational contributions, which may partially account for the deviations observed in the correlations. Our study is supported by experimental Raman spectra of isotopically enriched samples and theoretical simulations. Although this study focuses on carbon dioxide, similar behavior is expected for other series of isotopologues.
authors: Eduardo Su\'arez, Christian Ostertag-Henning, Miguel Carvajal, Renato Lemus

papers.title: Size-Dependent High-Order Harmonic Generation from Linear Carbon-Chain Molecules in Linearly Polarized Laser Fields
papers.abstract: High-order harmonic generation from molecules is highly sensitive to molecular geometry and strong-field electron dynamics, providing a powerful route for probing and controlling ultrafast processes in extended systems. In this work, we systematically investigate the influence of molecular chain length on HHG from linear carbon-chain molecules C$_2$H$_2$, C$_6$H$_2$, and C$_{10}$H$_2$ driven by an 800 nm linearly polarized laser field. To isolate the molecular-size effect from the influence of different ionization potentials, the laser intensities are adjusted to maintain the same Keldysh parameter for different molecules. Real-time time-dependent density functional theory simulations are performed with the molecular axis aligned parallel to the laser polarization direction. The results show that increasing the molecular chain length significantly enhances the harmonic yield and tends to extend the cutoff region. In particular, C$_{10}$H$_2$ exhibits much stronger plateau harmonics than C$_2$H$_2$, while the intermediate molecule C$_6$H$_2$ shows harmonic intensities between those of C$_2$H$_2$ and C$_{10}$H$_2$. Time-frequency analysis and charge-density evolution reveal that the enhanced HHG emission in longer chains originates from the enlarged electron acceleration distance and increased probability of multi-center recollision, especially near the terminal carbon atoms. These findings demonstrate that molecular-size engineering offers an effective strategy for controlling harmonic emission and optimizing attosecond light sources in extended molecular systems.
authors: Yifan Kang, Yang Yang, Yingtan Li, Shuwen Pang, Huiwen Yang, Yingdan Zhang, Shushan Zhou

papers.title: Realization Divergence in Multi-Provider Quantum Computing: A Pre-Registered Study of What Survives Measurement
papers.abstract: Quantum programs pass through compilers, transpilers and vendor services before execution. However, the distance between what was written and what runs is rarely measured. We call this distance realization divergence: the observable difference in how an identical source circuit is realized and behaves across quantum software stacks. We report a hardware study across three vendors and four devices, combining pre-registered predictions with explicitly identified exploratory analyses and amendments. In a compilation experiment with assigned placement policies, embedding radius correlates with two-qubit overhead at Spearman 0.805, against 0.492 for circuit size. Under a fixed lowest-index policy, an eight-qubit Bernstein-Vazirani circuit exhibits greater execution divergence than a twelve-qubit circuit on IQM Emerald. The opposite ordering occurs on IQM Garnet. Both comparisons replicate across two repetitions with disjoint confidence intervals. These results support a placement-dependent explanation, without isolating individual hardware noise mechanisms. The same ordering inversion is absent on the all-to-all IonQ control. On Rigetti Cepheus, a follow-up using topology-aware native placement found no consistent advantage in correct-answer probability for either submission track, but did not establish equivalence between the tracks. Structural comparisons depend on metric weighting, placement and device generation. Provider interfaces also limit observability: Rigetti's supported-operation list remained unchanged across a device generation that replaced the native entangler. We classify silent interface failures in composed toolchains and identify checks at toolchain boundaries, connecting valid cross-provider comparisons with concrete software-quality practices.
authors: Jouni Peltonen, Vlad Stirbu, Tommi Mikkonen

papers.title: Operator-Space Entanglement Entropy in Random Fermionic Gaussian Dynamics
papers.abstract: We study the von Neumann operator-space entanglement entropy (OSEE) of initial product operators evolved under random gaussian dynamics, as modeled by a Brownian SYK$_2$ model. By exploiting a mapping to a domain-wall melting problem, we derive an exact expression for the time-dependent bipartite OSEE in the thermodynamic limit, and obtain an analytic characterization of the corresponding gaussian Page curve emerging at late times. Our results build on recent work on the entanglement dynamics in the all-to-all quantum simple exclusion process, leveraging tools from RMT, including the Coulomb-gas approach and a mapping to the free Jacobi process. Finally, based on our results, we discuss the possibility of relating the OSEE with non-gaussianity measures in the Heisenberg picture.
authors: Pablo Bayona-Pena, Elena Gramellini, Lorenzo Piroli

papers.title: Multi-Higgs production from a theory of varying Higgs quartic and top Yukawa couplings
papers.abstract: We study the collider phenomenology of a theory in which the Higgs quartic self-coupling and the top Yukawa coupling are \textit{varying couplings}, which arise dynamically from two scalar fields, $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$. Depending on the scalar masses relative to twice the top-quark mass, the heavy scalars decay mainly to Higgs boson pairs ($hh$) or to top-quark pairs ($t\bar t$), giving two distinct signatures. We find sizeable cross sections for resonant $hh$ production, and also for the background-suppressed process with three Higgs bosons ($hhh$) from associated production, $pp \to h\phi_i \to hhh$. By recasting ATLAS resonance searches, we set bounds on the effective new-physics scales $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ at the TeV scale. We also show that the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) will probe this parameter space further, through combined measurements of the $hh$, $t\bar t$ and multi-Higgs channels. This gives a strong, multi-channel test of whether the electroweak sector has a dynamical origin.
authors: Ulf Danielsson, Rikard Enberg, Gunnar Ingelman, Soumyadip Kundu, Tanumoy Mandal, Subhadip Mitra

papers.title: Remote Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Entanglement Generation between Trapped Ions
papers.abstract: Distributing entanglement directly between error-corrected logical qubits is an important capability for scalable quantum networks. We propose a heralded protocol for generating remote entanglement between Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill qubits encoded in the motional modes of spatially separated trapped ions, using the internal electronic states to interface the motional qubits with emitted photons. We derive the protocol for single-rail and polarization photonic encodings and evaluate the effects of finite GKP squeezing, photon loss, photon recoil, motional heating, and motional dephasing on the decoded logical state. Moreover, we numerically analysed the fidelity of distributed logical Bell-pair fidelity. We find that one can achieve more than 95% of fidelity in the realistic situation. The protocol combines motional-control and photonic-networking operations that have already been demonstrated in trapped-ion experiments.
authors: Haruki Aoki, Kazufumi Tanji, Shohei Kiryu, Masahiro Takeoka, Junko Ishi-Hayase

papers.title: Probing Deconfined Quantum Criticality Point on a Digital Quantum Computer
papers.abstract: A deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) is a continuous transition between ordered phases with unrelated broken symmetries, beyond the Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm. In one dimension, such a transition between a $z$-polarized ferromagnet (zFM) and a valence-bond solid (VBS) is well established numerically in a frustrated spin-$1/2$ chain. Here we ask whether a superconducting quantum processor can resolve this transition and its signatures despite finite-size effects and device noise. The ground states are prepared by ancilla-projected quantum imaginary-time evolution (QITE), whose exact target states are compressed by tensor-network optimization into shallow depth quantum circuits. The hardware data distinguish the phases through their order parameters, spin and dimer correlations, structure factors, correlation ratios, and snapshot distributions. The crossing of the order parameters locates the transition, and its finite-size extrapolation lies close to the thermodynamic-limit value obtained from large-scale numerics. A noise model based on the device calibration accounts quantitatively for the reduced amplitudes measured on hardware. Our findings demonstrate that a Landau-forbidden transition between competing orders can be resolved on current quantum processors.
authors: Mrinal Kanti Giri, Pinaki Sengupta

papers.title: Local finite rate semi device independent randomness expansion from quantum contextuality
papers.abstract: Finite rate randomness expansion (RE) which is secure against quantum adversaries is a crucial information processing task which is well studied in the case of two non-communicating parties sharing Bell non-local correlations in a device independent manner. In this paper we show that contextual correlations with only a single localized party are sufficient for RE in a semi-device independent (SDI) manner. We propose a template SDI-RE protocol which is applicable for arbitrary $N$-cycle non-contextuality (NC) inequalities and derive its RE rate under finite statistics. As a special case, we also highlight the advantages of the situation when RE is constrained by Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality but with characterized measurements implemented by only a single party. Our template protocol also incorporates non-ideal statistics which may not satisfy perfect commutativity and perfect repeatability, both of which are necessary in a loophole-free test of NC inequalities. As such, several recent experimental implementations of significantly loophole-free tests of NC inequalities can be modified for secure RE following our approach.
authors: Dhananjoy Ghosh, Nandana J, Jaskaran Singh

papers.title: Localization induced by Sinai disorder in mass-exchange models
papers.abstract: We introduce a conservative continuous-mass-exchange model with quenched disorder in the splitting laws on the bonds of a finite segment. Although the dynamics is generically irreversible, its stationary mean mass profile remarkably turns out to be exactly solvable through an associated birth-and-death chain and has a Gibbs representation in terms of a simple random-walk potential. If $N$ is the number of bonds and $\beta$ measures the strength of disorder, the parameter $\beta\sqrt N$ separates an asymptotically flat profile, a Brownian crossover, and a profile localized near the global minimum. We characterize the fluctuations of macroscopic masses and identify arcsine laws for the localization centre, the competition between left and right valleys, and the disorder-averaged mass measure. Furthermore, for the extremal masses, we discuss the emergent limiting random variable in terms of the literature linking finite RW paths seen from its minimum to infinite-horizon walks conditioned to stay positive. Finally, in proximity of the localization transition point $\beta=0$, we show that the inverse participation ratio for the extremal masses give rises to a scaling with decay of order $k^{-3/2}$ consistent with the scaling limit of the latter conditioned walk. In the same limit, the inverse participation ratio shows a scaling form.
authors: Michele Giusfredi, Luca Avena, Paolo Politi

papers.title: Same Spectrum, Harder First-Order Training: Phase-Locking in Single- versus Multi-Qubit Re-Uploading Circuits
